title: Visibility & Cost: Trace Ownership and Dashboard Design Playbook
content:
Goal:
Provide a practical playbook that balances high-fidelity observability for inference pipelines with ingestion/retention cost limits. Define metric & trace ownership, sampling rules, dashboard composition conventions, and an alert prioritization heuristic so teams can make reproducible decisions when opening new signal surfaces or scaling retention.

Context and motivation:
- Inference workloads produce high-cardinality telemetry (model id, route, customer id, token length, batch size, hw type). Naively keeping full-resolution metrics/traces is expensive and hurts query latency.
- We want to avoid surprise bills and dashboard sprawl while preserving the ability to debug incidents quickly.
- This playbook is intended for infra/serving teams, product-owned model teams, and SREs who maintain production SLIs.

Success criteria (how we measure this playbook's impact):
- Mean time to root cause (MTTR) for latency regressions reduced by 20% for incidents that require cross-service traces.
- Ingest cost growth for telemetry limited to <10% QoQ while traffic grows 25% QoQ.
- No dashboard has more than 25 widgets unless owned/justified in docs.

Key principles:
1) Prioritize signal-oriented ownership: each metric/trace span needs a single owner (team) and a replacement strategy if a team disbands.
2) Cost-aware retention: default retention tiers with clear gating for longer retention.
3) Sampling as first-class: deterministic sampling rules tied to customer tier, route, and incident mode.
4) Dashboard minimalism: each dashboard must state intent, owner, and SLOs it supports.

Metrics catalog (recommended naming & minimal schema) - define fields we must collect and owners:
- inference.request.count
  - description: number of inference requests accepted by front door
  - unit: count
  - SLI: used for availability SLO
  - owner: product-hosted-api

- inference.request.latency.p50/p95/p99
  - description: end-to-end request latency measured at ingress returning final token or error
  - unit: ms
  - SLO target (example): p95 < 250ms for hosted-low-latency routes
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime

- model.kv_cache.hit_rate
  - description: ratio of KV cache hits to lookups (intra-request reuse)
  - unit: ratio
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime

- batching.batch_size.percentile (p50/p90)
  - description: observed batch sizes across GPUs for inference service
  - unit: items
  - owner: eng-serving-runtime

- gpu.utilization.avg
  - description: GPU utilization reported per machine-pool
  - unit: percent
  - owner: infra

- inference.cost.per_token_estimate
  - description: rolling estimate combining infra cost, GPU time, and model quantization factor
  - unit: USD/token
  - owner: finance + infra

Naming conventions: use dot-separated nouns, suffix percentiles (p95), and avoid embedding dashboard-specific context. All new metrics must include a one-line definition and an owner tag in the metric metadata.

Trace design and sampling rules:
- Span naming: service.operation.model_name.version (example: serving.generate.ggml-v2.1)
- Minimum span set to always collect in full (no sampling): request ingress, route decision, model selection, scheduler dispatch, GPU enqueue, model decode loop (summary span), response flush.
- Conditional detailed spans (sampled): token-level decode spans, KV-cache internal spans, per-chunk disk IO. These are high-cardinality and should be sampled at the following rates by default:
  - internal-prod-tier customers: 10% token-level sampling
  - host-tier (critical routes / canary): 100% for first 10 minutes after deploy, 20% steady-state
  - enterprise customers with dedicated capacity: 100% but routed to private trace retention (not central ingest)
- Rate-limited burst capture: on detection of a major latency or error SLO breach, flip into incident mode: increase sampling to 100% for affected trace ids for a bounded window (default 30 minutes) and store to short-term hot retention (72 hours). This is automated via rollout hooks.
- Deterministic sampling by trace key: ensure customer_id or request_id hashing-based decisions to retain proportional visibility across customers.

Dashboard composition and micro-SLI view pattern:
- Every dashboard must include header metadata: owner, intent, last_updated, primary_SLO, data_retention_tier.
- Micro-SLI view: for each SLO, provide a 3-tile group: (1) SLI trend (7d/30d), (2) SLI decomposition by most important dimension (route/model/hw), (3) top contributing traces/errors. Keep groups vertically stacked, 3–4 groups max per dashboard.
- Use drilldowns not single dashboards full of widgets. A single high-level dashboard should be lightweight and link to team-owned deep-dive dashboards.
- Card / widget limits: base dashboards <= 12 widgets. Deep-dive dashboards can go up to 30 if approved. Every extra widget must justify incremental debug value.

Alerting and prioritization heuristic:
- Alert categories: Critical (P1), High (P2), Medium (P3). Map to oncall rotations and paging rules.
- Example rules:
  - P1: SLI breach (p95 latency > target) sustained > 5 minutes AND error rate > 0.5% above baseline -> page oncall.
  - P2: Budget alerts (inbound telemetry ingestion exceeds expected by 30% QoQ) -> notify telemetry stewards.
  - P3: Dashboard drift (missing data, broken queries) -> ticket created for owners.
- Alert suppression: if a canary roll is in-progress, suppress P2 pager noise and route to a deploy-specific channel with auto-comment.

Ownership & runbooks:
- Each metric/trace/span and dashboard must list a single owner (email alias recommended). On ownership transfer, a short migration doc must be attached in the metric metadata.
- Runbook template (must be attached to dashboards that support SLOs):
  1) Short description and expected behavior
  2) Where to look first (3 bullets)
  3) Known false positives and how to silence them
  4) Incident playbook (links to deeper traces, runbooks for rollbacks)
  5) After-action checklist (include signal retention decisions)

Cost controls and retention tiers (defaults):
- Fast-hot (default for SLO & critical traces): 7 days full fidelity, hot storage for traces up to 72 hours.
- Warm: 30 days aggregated metrics (no token-level traces), sampling 5–10% for traces.
- Cold: 90 days aggregated metrics only, no traces unless specifically archived by legal/compliance.
- Long-term archive: >90 days only by explicit export (parquet to S3) with approval to limit egress.
- Cardinatlity controls: enforce tag whitelists for high-volume spans (customer_id only for enterprise tier, otherwise bucketize customer_id to coarse groups).

Cost guardrails to implement now (short term):
- Per-team telemetry budget that resets monthly; teams must request quota increases with justification (link to cost playbook).
- Autosampling throttle: when total trace ingest > budget threshold, automatically reduce token-level sampling across non-high-priority routes.
- Dashboard audit every quarter: remove stale widgets and consolidate overlapping dashboards.

Example queries & troubleshooting recipes (pseudocode):
- Find p95 latency regression root-cause:
  1) Query: SELECT p95(latency) by route, model_name over last 6h vs previous 6h
  2) If model_name shows delta, filter traces for model_name and aggregate by gpu_pool and batch_size.
  3) If GPU pool shows spike, inspect gpu.utilization.avg and scheduler wait spans.

- Tokenization blowup detection:
  1) Query batch_size percentile and request.token_count percentiles, correlate with exit codes and user prompt size.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Do we standardize a single telemetry budget per team or per service? (Pros/cons in appendix)
- What privacy constraints do we enforce for customer_id in traces across hosted vs private?
- Who approves retention >90 days for SLO-related traces? Current suggestion: Security + Compliance + Product signoff.

Action items (next 60 days):
- [ ] Telemetry config: implement default sampling rules in ingest pipeline (assigned: Marco)
- [ ] Dashboard header enforcement: small lint rule (assigned: Sofia)
- [ ] Runbook template in Confluence and linked to dashboards (assigned: Lena)
- [ ] Quarterly audit kickoff: schedule with owners and SRE (assigned: Observability PM)

References and helpful links:
- Confluence page: Observability standards (CONFLUENCE-OBS-1234)
- Telemetry config repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry
- Cost playbook: FIN-COST-TELEMETRY-REQS (internal)

Notes to self: keep this playbook opinionated — we will iterate. Focus the first implementation on the hosted API routes that generate the majority of ingest cost.

Revision history:
- 2025-11-04 created initial draft
- 2026-01-12 added retention tiers and sampling default rates after sync with finance
- 2026-02-20 updated runbook template and added action items

Unresolved: finalize enterprise privacy policy for tracing and add approved regexes for tag whitelists.
